body: Priya is a third-year medical student on a clinical placement in a busy general practice. After a consultation ends, a patient approaches Priya privately in the corridor and asks her to pass a personal message to the GP. The patient explains they were too embarrassed to mention a symptom during the consultation but now feels it might be important. The message contains details of a new and potentially significant symptom.

situational_judgement_questions.question_text: Priya takes note of the message and passes it to the GP promptly, suggesting the GP may wish to follow up with the patient.
situational_judgement_questions.correct_answer: A very appropriate thing to do
situational_judgement_questions.answer_reason: Passing clinically relevant information to the responsible clinician promptly is a core patient safety responsibility. Priya cannot assess the significance of the symptom herself, and ensuring the GP receives the information maintains proper clinical oversight.
